subject: a Burning fire damage-over-time status-effect glyph for an ARPG buff bar
bestPrompt: A single Burning fire damage-over-time status glyph for an ARPG buff bar, designed to fill a SQUARE icon frame edge-to-edge as one bold chunky emblem, legible at 32px, flame alone on a near-black field, no border. Subject identity: a compact stout flame erupting from a CHARRED CRACKED EMBER BASE — blackened coals veined with glowing molten-orange lava cracks at the bottom, the burning fuel that signals a lingering damage-over-time affliction. Art style: the grim painterly buff-icon craft of Path of Exile 2, Diablo IV and Hades II — sculpted hand-painted rendering with real material weight and grime, tactile charcoal texture on the coals, thick painterly heat in the flame. Value ramp: a tight searing white-hot core low in the flame, blooming amber and molten orange, cooling to deep crimson tongues with sharp curling tips and a thin dark smoke wisp above. A scatter of bright flying embers and sparks lifts off the flame — the active-burning cue. Strong specular rim-light sculpts the coals and flame edges so the shape snaps off the dark field with crisp hard silhouette, no fuzzy halo. High craft, painterly AAA icon polish, rich material. NOT a flat vector emoji, NOT cel-shaded color-fill, NOT dark-outlined coloring-book banding, NOT a smooth sticker, NOT a cartoon flame, NOT a photograph. Absolutely NO text, NO letters, NO watermark, NO signature.
technique: The breakthrough lever on Lucid Origin is giving the effect a TEXTURED MATERIAL SUBSTRATE, not just fire. Five prompts describing the flame alone — however hard they pushed 'impasto / hand-painted / semi-transparent overlapping tongues' — all stalled at 60-66 because the judge persistently reads Lucid Origin's flame interior as flat cel-shaded banding (materialRendering pinned 55-62). Adding a 'charred cracked ember base veined with glowing molten-orange lava cracks' gave the model real grime and charcoal texture to render, which jumped materialRendering 58->70, edgeQuality 66->77, valueHierarchy to 80, styleCohesion 68->75, total 66->72. Supporting levers (all necessary, none sufficient alone): hard anti-vector negatives (NOT flat vector emoji / cel-shaded color-fill / coloring-book banding), a named continuous value ramp (white-hot core -> amber -> crimson), a DoT identity cue (lava cracks + rising embers), explicit anti-halo edge instruction, and hard text/watermark negatives (cleanliness 90-95 every run).

iterations.note: Painterly oil/gouache single flame, named value ramp, anti-vector negatives. Cleanliness 95, but material 62 — judge calls it a generic soft-gradient stock flame with fuzzy contour bleed and no DoT identity.
Pushed toward crisp graphic/flatter icon language + ember cluster. Backfired — read as a cartoon messaging-app flame; material 55, styleCohesion 58. Painterly beats graphic on this model.
Painterly flame inside a subtle beveled iron badge frame. Frame lifted styleCohesion to 70 but was the weak link — judge saw a flat drop-shadow disc, not a forged bezel; material fell to 58.
No frame, painterly flame + smoky charred tips + rising ember trail (DoT cue) + anti-halo. Value 78 but judge still reads interior as cel-shaded color-blob; material 58 — the pure-flame ceiling.

Reframed as many semi-transparent overlapping additive-glow tongues to defeat the flat interior. Model still flattened it to banded fill; material 60. Confirms pure-flame material is capped ~62 on Lucid Origin.

WINNER — charred cracked ember base with glowing lava cracks gave the model textured material to render. material 70, edge 77, value 80, style 75. Remaining knock: two-part flame+rock scene, silhouette 68 (base collapses to a dark mass at 32px).
